release_notes:
# Vidrick AI Transcriber 4.3 — Long-recording update

- Memory-efficient transcription preprocessing retains the same recognition
  settings and whole-recording audio normalization, with bounded FFT work.
- Long recordings use bounded speaker-analysis windows and learned voice
  comparisons across the recording. Automatic mode does not assume a fixed
  number of people. Requested counts guide global matching, but conflicting
  or insufficient voice evidence is left for review instead of being forced
  into that total.
- In long recordings, speech without sufficient identity evidence is marked **Uncertain speaker
  (review)** instead of being presented as another confirmed person. This
  review category can contain multiple people. The app also reports when a
  requested speaker count cannot be satisfied. Speaker labels still need
  review, particularly for overlapping or noisy speech.
- The transcription model is released before speaker identification, and CPU
  worker allocation is reduced on low-memory machines.
- Progress follows actual processing stages. Transcription estimates no longer
  carry into speaker identification; expired and sleep-interrupted countdowns
  are cleared. Speaker stages report completed work or show an activity
  indicator when their remaining duration is unknown. Each file in a batch
  starts with fresh progress and estimates.
- Optional local performance diagnostics record timings and memory usage
  without including audio, transcript text or source filenames.
- Subtitle timestamps now round correctly across second and minute boundaries.
- Speaker overlap resolution preserves exact timestamp boundaries, fixing a
  precision error that could stretch a brief speaker label across a much
  longer neighboring passage.

The existing local ONNX speaker engine remains in use; no new cloud audio
service, account, or speaker-model download is introduced.

Performance and speaker accuracy depend on hardware and recording conditions.
Validation includes independent public recordings, annotated speaker checks,
fresh transcription and speaker processing, and separate corrected export
replays. These checks do not establish performance on a physical 8 GB machine
or constitute a fresh-machine GUI installation test. Matching the expected
speaker count alone is not a verified accuracy score.
